## Research question
How does Glimmer compare with Trellis-RE across the three relation-extraction test sets, and what does the ablation show about the evidence-gating module?

## Methods summary
Glimmer is a document-level relation extractor that adds an evidence-gating module, which down-weights sentences judged irrelevant to an entity pair, on top of a Trellis-RE-style encoder. Trellis-RE is the main baseline. 'Glimmer w/o evidence gating' removes only the gating module. All systems are trained on Hollin-DocRE only.

## Experimental setup
Hollin-DocRE is the in-domain test set; Saltmarsh-Bio (biomedical) and Wistmoor-News (news) are out-of-domain test sets not used for training or tuning. Metric: relation F1 (%, higher is better), mean over 3 seeds; the seed standard deviation is at most 0.4 F1 for every entry.

## Experiments and comparisons
- `exp1`: Main comparison and ablation on three test sets
  - comparison `exp1/cmp1`: Glimmer (full) vs Trellis-RE: F1 per test set
  - comparison `exp1/cmp2`: Glimmer (full) vs Glimmer w/o evidence gating: F1 per test set (ablation)

sentences.text: Glimmer (full) achieves higher relation F1 than Trellis-RE on Hollin-DocRE (65.2% vs 61.8%) and Saltmarsh-Bio (55.9% vs 52.3%), but lower F1 on Wistmoor-News (69.2% vs 70.0%).
Removing the evidence-gating module decreases F1 on Hollin-DocRE (63.0% vs 65.2%) and Saltmarsh-Bio (54.1% vs 55.9%), but increases F1 on Wistmoor-News (72.4% vs 69.2%).
Thus, the evidence-gating module's benefit is inconsistent across domains: it improves performance in the in-domain and biomedical settings but hurts performance on the news test set.
No statistical tests were reported, so these differences may not be significant.

Glimmer outperforms Trellis-RE on the in-domain Hollin-DocRE set (65.2% vs. 61.8% F1) and on the biomedical Saltmarsh-Bio set (55.9% vs. 52.3% F1), but underperforms on the news Wistmoor-News set (69.2% vs. 70.0% F1).

The ablation shows that removing the evidence-gating module reduces F1 on Hollin-DocRE (from 65.2% to 63.0%) and Saltmarsh-Bio (from 55.9% to 54.1%), but increases F1 on Wistmoor-News (from 69.2% to 72.4%).
No statistical tests were reported, so the observed differences cannot be characterized as significant or reliable.

All systems were trained solely on Hollin-DocRE.
